writtenBefore: any verdict count, score, rate or paired comparison of this run was computed. What had been seen: the orchestrator's identity record and README (run facts, stop code, label-read counts and receipt statistics; no per-case verdicts), the ledgers' structure and stop rows, and the Q-497363 trial 1 receipt. No score.py or analyze.py output existed and no report had been read for content.

integrity.checkedByMe: Independently of the orchestrator, with the committed verifier verify_gemini_run.py (commit 9102756 or later) run on a working directory reassembled from the returned archive: both ledgers have 64 rows in the frozen submission order, no case missing or duplicated; every row carries the run's stamp (route native-flash-high, parser snapshot-label-tolerant, run manifest d853fee3..., binary 16e228cb..., trial number); every ledger report hash equals the SHA-256 of the returned report (127 of 127) and the receipt's report hash; re-parsing every report with the committed tolerant parser reproduces every ledger row, every label-read flag and the absence of any other stop; every one of the 127 clean receipts says REPORT_RECEIVED_PENDING_ADJUDICATION with no failure or closing failure, model gemini-3.8-flash-high, effort high, zero retries, one proxy and one native invocation, both processes reaped, private home and socket directory absent, native binary hash equal to the pinned one, and prompt delivery COMPLETE with wireBytes and bytesWritten equal to the length of the stream-json frame for the corpus-derived prompt of that case. The verifier reports no failures for either trial.
integrity.limitsOfTheCheck: The returned archive is hand-assembled (ledger, reports, receipts, identity, qualification record) and does not contain the per-case packets or the CLI init and prompt files. The verifier's REQUEST_MISMATCH check therefore ran against packets regenerated from the committed corpus and is vacuous here; the request is bound only by the receipts' wireBytes, which equal the expected frame length for every case, and by the run manifest and corpus hashes in every row. Process reaping and sandbox isolation are the receipts' statements and were not independently re-run. The offline qualification (664 cases, two passes) is the orchestrator's record. The served model is not attested: every receipt says servedAttestation UNAVAILABLE and effortEvidence launcher_configuration.
integrity.orchestratorVerifierNote: The orchestrator ran the verifier at run commit 58a7b38, which still compared the receipt's wireBytes with the bare prompt length, so its log lists PROMPT_DELIVERY for every case of trial 1. That was a defect in the verifier (the runtime sends the prompt as one stream-json frame, 71 bytes longer for these prompts), fixed in 9102756 and validated on the 48 receipts of the Gemini v1 pilot before this run; the orchestrator correctly stopped and edited nothing. The fixed verifier shows no such failure on either trial here.
integrity.orchestratorBehaviour: This time the orchestrator did not commit or push; the evidence reached this repository only as the returned archive. The identity record gives the run commit 58a7b38219b6930b232695842292c10918011809, which is a commit of this repository.

stopsDocumentation.cause: The receipt records status STOPPED, failure UNQUALIFIED_STEP, prompt delivery COMPLETE (2734 of 2734 bytes), one proxy and one native invocation, both reaped, 471.7 seconds elapsed (the 600 second limit was not reached), and an event ledger of init, user_input DONE, agent_response DONE (307 bytes), then a step of type error_message DONE (175 bytes); no report was written (report: null). The runtime treats any step type outside its qualified set as a stop, and an error_message step is one. The content of the error and of the 307-byte agent_response is not in the returned archive (the receipt stores event kinds and sizes only), so the cause of the model-side error is not known. The same case drew a normal report in trial 2.
stopsDocumentation.headline: The as-run result is the headline: this observation is a technical stop, is removed from every denominator, and is not counted as a verdict or as a wrong judgment. It is not rerun (a recorded case is never rerun).
stopsDocumentation.documentedRuleView: None. The only relaxation (a snapshot label S01:<n> in the line field of a FINDING is read as line n) was preregistered for this run, is built into the parser that produced the ledgers, and is reported as a count (3 observations in trial 1, 8 in trial 2). There is no format stop in either trial, so there is no second documented-rule view and none is computed.
stopsDocumentation.sensitivityNote: Because there is only one stop and no report to reclassify, no reclassification is possible. A bounding sensitivity (the stopped observation counted as each of the other outcomes) is possible but is not part of the preregistration and is not added.

noOtherExclusion: No pair, family, case or observation is excluded or reclassified. The output-byte exclusion of the v1 pilot does not apply: corpus v3 has no such family. The corpus audit's reclassifications (audit/classification.json) are part of the frozen corpus and already in the oracle.
readingPlan: After the scores are computed, the preregistered reading: every evidence-gap twin not judged GO_WITH_CHANGES, every defect twin without NO_GO, every sound plan not judged GO, and a sample of up to ten correct evidence-gap twins, classified by whether the report names the planted gap or defect and what it does with it. The reader is the corpus author, who has seen the scores. The reading can add observations about the reviewer; it cannot change the as-run numbers.
